- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then overshoot, particularly after sharp upward spikes in the history.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — overestimates after recent high prices and underestimates after recent lows.
- Forecasts are generally too optimistic in the 10–20 day window, often missing the true mean or trending downward.
- Model fails to adjust for recent volatility clustering — overreacts to short-term spikes without sufficient decay.
- Forecasts show persistent lag in capturing true price momentum, especially in the 20–30 day window.
- Model underestimates the true price range in the final 5–10 days, often missing the upward correction or final spike.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fail to capture sudden reversals or sharp corrections in the last 5–10 days.
- Model tends to overfit recent history, especially when prices are trending upward, leading to over-optimistic forecasts.
- Forecasts are too conservative in the final 5–10 days, often underestimating the true price range or final spike.
